description: RISE used IESVE during preliminary design of a hospital in southern Italy to compare water-cooled and air-cooled chillers. The model represented outdoor-air treatment, humidity control, heat recovery and hot-water loops. The account compares energy costs, capital costs and cooling-tower water demand. Although the water-cooled design used less energy, the source reports choosing air cooling because of limited water availability. The hospital is unnamed. The source reports an energy reduction with the unit kW, so no corrected numerical energy figure is invented. Model outputs do not establish built-system performance. This public HTML case narrative is published by IES and can be read without payment. Its reuse licence is not stated. Access to the described software, input data and project models is not established by the public page. The source does not give a complete study period or all spatial and temporal model resolutions. Reported results are provider claims and have not been independently reproduced. The case supports the documented infrastructure simulation use and is linked to the named modelling resources. Only metadata and the case description were inspected; no data or model files were downloaded.
